The History of Toledo City Science High School

Ilihan comes from "Alihan," which means to barricade. During World War II, Filipino guerrillas built foxholes and stone shields here to defend themselves from Japanese forces. Today, the same ground shelters students instead.

  1. World War IIFilipino guerrillas built foxholes and stone shields at Alihan to defend themselves from Japanese forces.
  2. 1996Answering a DepEd initiative for specialized science and math instruction, the school opened with 25 first-year students.
  3. The early yearsThe school was annexed to Bato National High School, the lead school under the Schools Division of Toledo City.

    Our community

    Our four houses

    Our houses are named for the four pillars of STEM: science, technology, engineering and mathematics.

    Scire

    Science

    From the Latin for "to know".

    Techne

    Technology

    From the Greek for "craft" and "skill".

    Handasa

    Engineering

    From the Arabic word for "engineering".

    Manthanein

    Mathematics

    From the Greek for "to learn".

    News and updates

    The latest from Toledo City Science High School.

    Achievement

    TCSHS wins 1st Grand Award at NSEF 2026

    Toledo City Science High School (TCSHS) proudly claims the 1st Grand Award in the Science News Video Report at the National Science and Engineering Fair (NSEF) 2026!

    With this year's theme, "STEM in Action: Innovating a Better World," our team showcased creativity, communication and technological skills on a virtual stage, proving that innovation knows no boundaries.

    Team members

    • Director: Wynnie Bryle Gaña
    • Presenter: Sheryfina Castaños
    • Videographer and Editor: Lemuel Presente
    • Coach: Virgie Lee Deligero

    This achievement is a testament to our teamwork, dedication and passion for science and innovation. Congratulations, TCSHS! The future is STEM, and we're putting it into action!

    Math

    Our Mathletes shine at the PAMES-CASIO Math Challenge

    Congratulations to our TCSHS Mathletes for securing multiple wins at the PAMES-CASIO Math Challenge.
